source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: The official e-Shram FAQ describes e-Shram as the Ministry of Labour and Employment's integrated national database of unorganised workers. Registration creates a permanent 12-digit Universal Account Number, or UAN, intended to help workers access government schemes, entitlements and services. Once assigned, the UAN remains unchanged for the worker.
title: e-Shram - purpose and UAN

source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: The official FAQ says a person engaged in unorganised work who is aged 16 years or older may register on the e-Shram portal, subject to the other prescribed registration criteria. It identifies home-based workers, self-employed workers and wage workers in the unorganised sector as unorganised workers.
title: e-Shram - registration eligibility

source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: For e-Shram registration, the official FAQ lists an Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked mobile number. A worker without an Aadhaar-linked mobile number may register through biometric authentication at a Common Service Centre or State Seva Kendra. A worker may self-register on the e-Shram portal or use assisted registration at a CSC. Registration is free, and the FAQ says workers should not pay a registration charge. At a CSC, the worker does not need to submit documents but should carry the Aadhaar number and mobile phone for registration.
title: e-Shram - documents, registration routes and fee

source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: The official FAQ says workers may update their e-Shram details through the portal or a CSC. For a portal update, the worker logs in using the UAN and the OTP sent to the registered mobile number, edits details such as address, contact number, bank-account information or occupation, saves the changes, and completes any required OTP or email verification. A worker changing the registered mobile number may use 'Update profile using Aadhaar' under the 'Already registered' menu, or visit a CSC or State Seva Kendra when an Aadhaar-registered mobile number is unavailable.
title: e-Shram - update profile and mobile number

section: Using One-Stop Solution after existing registration
source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: The official FAQ says an existing e-Shram registrant does not need to register again for e-Shram One-Stop Solution. The worker may use the existing UAN to log in and monitor enrolled schemes. On a scheme listing, an 'Apply' button indicates that the user is not enrolled and may start enrolment, while a 'View' button indicates existing enrolment and opens details or benefit tracking.
title: e-Shram One-Stop Solution - existing registrants and scheme status

source_authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India
text: If the e-Shram portal is not working or has a technical issue, the official FAQ recommends checking the internet connection, refreshing the page, clearing browser cache and cookies, trying another browser or device, and then contacting the e-Shram helpdesk at 14434 if the issue remains. The FAQ identifies 14434 as the national helpdesk for registration and service queries and advises trying again later or using the portal's grievance option if the line is temporarily unreachable.
title: e-Shram - technical support and helpdesk
